Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.tuner

Class PitchDetector

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.tuner.PitchDetector
public final class PitchDetector extends Object
A time-domain fundamental-frequency estimator using the YIN algorithm (de Cheveigné & Kawahara, 2002), the standard autocorrelation-based pitch detector for monophonic instrument tuning.

It runs entirely on a float[] sample buffer - no AWT, no audio device, no threads, no Java 3D - so a detector can be fed a synthetic sine wave of a known frequency and asserted on headless. The microphone capture that fills those buffers lives in TunerPanel.

The five YIN steps are implemented directly:

  1. Difference function d(tau) = sum_j (x[j] - x[j+tau])^2.
  2. Cumulative mean normalised difference so the value is scale-free: d'(tau) = d(tau) / ((1/tau) * sum_{k<=tau} d(k)), with d'(0) = 1.
  3. Absolute threshold: the first lag whose d' drops below a threshold, refined down to the following local minimum.
  4. Parabolic interpolation around that lag for sub-sample accuracy.
  5. Frequency f0 = sampleRate / tau.

The lag search is bounded to the guitar/bass range (30.0f..1200.0f Hz), which also caps the O(W²) work, and a low RMS noise floor rejects silence so a quiet room never reports a spurious pitch.
